headline: High: shared networked, MCP-enabled document workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-cascade risks; compliance risk is moderate due to financial data and third-party APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a ingests web/API content and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while agent_b can run browsers and use MCP, so a content bridge exists where attacker-controlled text from A can be fed into B. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so prompt injection is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into agent_b prompts or MCP inputs
IF agent_b browser-sourced text is treated as instructions
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw agent_a outputs into agent_b
Add a provenance tag to all imported text
Restrict agent_b MCP tools to allowlisted sources
Review browser-scraped content before prompting
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; agent_b also has broad egress and can call many third-party model APIs. If either agent forwards shared workspace content or context, sensitive data can leave the pair through external services.
conditions: IF financial or market data is placed into agent_b prompts or files
IF either agent sends workspace contents to external APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared folders
Use separate API keys per agent
Turn off external API calls for sensitive runs
Redact financial identifiers before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad network egress, and agent_b can use MCP while agent_a can write files under .dexter/scratchpad/. That creates overlapping mutable surfaces and coordination risk, though the profiles do not show unrestricted shared filesystem writes or git access, so high is not justified.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace directory
IF an MCP tool exposes shared mutable state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid shared MCP resources for both agents
Check for concurrent edits before saving
requires-engineering: add transactional locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is an autonomous research agent that can emit market-related outputs, and agent_b is a document-processing agent with natural-language command handling and visualization. If B consumes A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions; the profiles do not prove direct action-taking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output without verification
IF agent_a-generated facts are rendered into diagrams or reports
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Ask agent_b to cite source documents separately
Compare A outputs against original inputs
Flag low-confidence claims before rendering
requires-engineering: add verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches financial data and uses third-party APIs, while agent_b processes documents and can also send data to multiple external model providers. This creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch or disclosure issue for regulated financial content, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdictional violation, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is routed through external APIs
IF retention policies differ across the two agents' providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of third-party APIs
Use provider settings with minimal retention
Document which data class each agent may process
Separate compliant and non-compliant workflows
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
